message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the main train stations in Miami that are known to be pet‑friendly (i.e., they allow pets on the premises, though there may be some rules such as leashing or size limits). If you’re planning a trip, it’s always a good idea to double‑check the latest policies directly with the station or the train operator (Amtrak) before you head out. | Train Station | Location & Notes | Pet Policy Highlights | |---------------|------------------|-----------------------| | **Miami Central Station (Miami Intermodal Center)** | 1 Seaboard Ave W, Miami, FL 33131 – the hub that connects Amtrak, Tri-Rail, Metrorail, and local buses. | • Pets are allowed in the station building and on the platforms.
• Must be on a leash or in a carrier.
• No pets in the waiting area during peak hours (check the station’s posted signs). | | **Miami Airport Station** | 1 Seaboard Ave W, Miami, FL 33131 – located just outside the airport terminal. | • Pets are permitted in the station and on the platform.
• Leash required; small dogs in carriers are fine.
• No pets in the ticketing office during busy times. | | **Miami Beach Station** | 1 Seaboard Ave W, Miami, FL 33131 – serves the South Florida Regional Transportation Authority (SFRTA) commuter rail. | • Pets are allowed on the platform and in the station.
• Must be on a leash or in a carrier.
• No pets in the ticket office during rush hour. | | **Doral Station** | 1 Seaboard Ave W, Doral, FL 33178 – part of the SFRTA commuter rail network. | • Pets are allowed in the station and on the platform.
• Leashed or in a carrier.
• No pets in the ticket office during peak times. | ### Quick Tips for Traveling with Pets in Miami Train Stations 1. **Check the Operator’s Rules** – Amtrak allows pets on board (usually up to two per passenger, with a fee for larger animals). The station itself typically follows the same leashing/carrier rules as the train. 2. **Leash or Carrier** – Most stations require pets to be on a leash or in a carrier while inside the station building or on the platform. 3. **Avoid Peak Hours** – Some stations restrict pets in the ticketing office during rush hour to keep the environment comfortable for all passengers. 4. **Clean Up** – Bring waste bags and clean up after your pet to keep the station tidy and friendly for everyone. If you need more detailed information (e.g., exact size limits, fees, or special accommodations), let me know which station you’re interested in, and I can dig up the most recent policy details for you!
